title: Addon-docs: Restore `docs.components` overrides for doc blocks
body:
Closes #

## What I did

- restored `docs.components` overrides for Storybook doc blocks that are imported in MDX or used internally by autodocs/docs pages
- introduced a shared `withMdxComponentOverride` helper and applied it across the relevant docs blocks
- fixed attached MDX docs pages so they respect the attached CSF file's `parameters.docs`, which makes the documented MDX component override flow work there too
- added a `Docs2/ComponentOverrides` CSF+MDX manual verification fixture that renders recognizable override markers for the overridden blocks
- this matches the behavior described in the current docs page for MDX component overrides: https://storybook.js.org/docs/configure/user-interface/theming#mdx-component-overrides

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

#### The changes in this PR are covered in the following automated tests:

- [ ] stories
- [x] unit tests
- [ ] integration tests
- [ ] end-to-end tests

#### Manual testing

> [!CAUTION]
> This section is mandatory for all contributions. If you believe no manual test is necessary, please state so explicitly. Thanks!

1. Run Storybook for the addon-docs template stories.
2. Open `https://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/addons-docs-blocks-component-overrides--mdx`.
3. Verify the autodocs page renders `override:*` markers for blocks like `Title`, `Subtitle`, `Primary`, `Controls`, and `Stories` instead of the default block UI.
4. Open the attached `MDX` entry for `Docs2/ComponentOverrides`.
5. Verify the imported doc blocks there also render `override:*` markers, confirming `docs.components` now applies to imported blocks like `Canvas`, `Story`, `Source`, and friends.

See deployed stories:https://635781f3500dd2c49e189caf-ahwwtndcxh.chromatic.com/?path=/docs/addons-docs-blocks-component-overrides--mdx

comments.author: coderabbitai
comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Delegating overrides recurse through the wrapped export.**

`withMdxComponentOverride()` re-reads `components.Title` on every render, so an override that composes with the public block (`components.Title = (props) => <Title {...props} />`) now loops forever: `Title -> Override -> Title -> …`. Before this change, importing `Title` inside the override bypassed MDX resolution. Please add a re-entry escape hatch in `code/addons/docs/src/blocks/blocks/withMdxComponentOverride.tsx`; the current `Override !== WrappedBlock` guard only handles `components.Title = Title`. The new manual fixture also won’t catch this because its overrides never render the public block from inside the override.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/addons/docs/src/blocks/blocks/Title.tsx` at line 55,
withMdxComponentOverride is causing infinite recursion when an override renders
the public export (e.g., components.Title = props => <Title {...props} />)
because the runtime re-resolves components.Title each render; to fix, add a
re-entry escape hatch in withMdxComponentOverride.tsx: define a module-level
Symbol (e.g., MDX_WRAPPED_BLOCK) and set it on the WrappedBlock export
(WrappedBlock[MDX_WRAPPED_BLOCK] = true), then when resolving components[name]
inside withMdxComponentOverride check if the resolved Override === WrappedBlock
OR if typeof Override === 'function' && Override[MDX_WRAPPED_BLOCK] is true and
in that case return WrappedBlock directly (skip MDX re-resolution/wrapping);
ensure you reference withMdxComponentOverride, WrappedBlock and Override in the
change so overrides that compose with the public block no longer recurse.
```

</details>

comments.author: coderabbitai
comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Allow overrides to target other wrapped docs blocks.**

Line 30 rejects *any* component that has already been wrapped by `withMdxComponentOverride`, so a valid override like `docs.components.Title = Subtitle` is ignored and falls back to the original block. The `wrappedBlocks` set plus `Override === WrappedBlock` already prevents self-recursion; this extra check blocks legitimate cross-block overrides. A small regression test around `components.Title = Subtitle` would lock this down.


<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
     if (
       wrappedBlocks?.has(blockName) ||
-      Override === WrappedBlock ||
-      (typeof Override === 'function' && Override[MDX_WRAPPED_BLOCK])
+      Override === WrappedBlock
     ) {
       return <Block {...props} />;
     }
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/addons/docs/src/blocks/blocks/withMdxComponentOverride.tsx` around lines
27 - 31, The conditional in withMdxComponentOverride incorrectly rejects any
function where Override[MDX_WRAPPED_BLOCK] is truthy, blocking valid cross-block
overrides (e.g., docs.components.Title = Subtitle); update the if condition in
withMdxComponentOverride to stop treating "is a wrapped component" as a
rejection—remove the (typeof Override === 'function' &&
Override[MDX_WRAPPED_BLOCK]) clause so only wrappedBlocks.has(blockName) and
Override === WrappedBlock prevent wrapping, and add a regression test that sets
components.Title = Subtitle to ensure cross-block overrides work.
```

</details>

<!-- fingerprinting:phantom:medusa:grasshopper -->

✅ Addressed in commit 0966221

comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_

**Story references `Basic` and `Secondary` do not exist.**

Lines 38-41 reference `ComponentOverrideStories.Basic` and `ComponentOverrideStories.Secondary`, but the stories file only exports `UsesDefaultImplementation`, `UsesMdxOverride`, `FallsBackWhenOverrideIsWrappedBlock`, `FallsBackWhenOverrideComposesPublicBlock`, and `AllowsDifferentWrappedBlockOverride`. This will cause runtime errors when rendering the MDX page.


<details>
<summary>🐛 Update to use existing story exports</summary>

```diff
-<Story of={ComponentOverrideStories.Basic} />
-<Canvas of={ComponentOverrideStories.Basic} />
-<Source of={ComponentOverrideStories.Basic} />
-<DocsStory of={ComponentOverrideStories.Secondary} />
+<Story of={ComponentOverrideStories.UsesDefaultImplementation} />
+<Canvas of={ComponentOverrideStories.UsesDefaultImplementation} />
+<Source of={ComponentOverrideStories.UsesDefaultImplementation} />
+<DocsStory of={ComponentOverrideStories.UsesMdxOverride} />
```
</details>

Alternatively, add `Basic` and `Secondary` exports to the stories file.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: Ok I think I get it now. Because we're not aliasing but swapping at runtime, the real implem inside an override must be preserved. The presence of the React context lets you detect that we've already overridden once, so any remaining block found in children is likely to be called by the override. Do we have _any_ possible with our existing blocks to have this code pattern though? ```jsx Foo ``` If we want to ensure we only skip overrides for A in the context of rendering A's own children, shouldn't you start from an empty set for each context provider, instead of appending to the parent set?
